intervals.quote: On 27 January 1971, two beams of protons collided in the Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) for the first time.

intervals.note: End from the same page: 'The ISR began operation in 1971 and ran until 1984'; year precision. Terminal event: the end of the operating interval above.
intervals.quote: On 27 January 1971, two beams of protons collided in the Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) for the first time.

name: Intersecting Storage Rings
notes: Per-ring energy: the earlier derived figure (about 31 GeV, half of 62 GeV) is replaced by the sourced 31.4 GeV/c of Bryant (arXiv:1206.3950); CERN's ISR page quotes only the 62 GeV maximum centre-of-mass energy.

beam_energy.note: A momentum (GeV/c) for protons; replaces the earlier half-of-62-GeV derivation (about 31 GeV). "Much of the operating life of the ISR was at 31.4 GeV/c, the maximum energy the magnet system could reach." (same paper).
beam_energy.quote: The CERN PS injected 26 GeV/c proton beams into the two rings that could accelerate up to 31.4 GeV/c.

cms_energy.quote: Protons circulated in opposite directions and collided with a maximum centre-of-mass energy of 62 GeV.

diameter.quote: The ISR was composed of two interlaced rings each with a diameter of 300 metres.

injection_energy.quote: The CERN PS injected 26 GeV/c proton beams into the two rings that could accelerate up to 31.4 GeV/c.

summary.plain: The world's first machine to collide two beams of protons head-on, built at CERN and running from 1971 to 1984. It convinced physicists that colliding hadrons could work, and it held the record for collision rate among hadron colliders until 2004.
summary.technical: Two interlaced proton storage rings, each 300 m in diameter, reaching 62 GeV centre-of-mass energy; first hadron collider, operated 1971-1984 and holder of the hadron-collider luminosity record until 2004.
